subject: Slice sampler error with negative values for Poisson and binomial- IPM

messages.subject: Slice sampler error with negative values for Poisson and binomial- IPM
parts:
Hi,
I'm putting together an Integrated Population Model, and nimble is returning negative values from the slice sampler along with the following error message:
"Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions for 'N[10, 16]'. Current parameter value is -5039." where N is a matrix of abundance values sampled with either a binomial or Poisson distribution. I tried increasing the maximum contractions from 100 (default) to 500 but the problems continue. 

AFSS <- configureMCMC(cmod, monitors=params, onlyRW=T, 
                      multivariateNodesAsScalars=T,
                      maxContractions=500)
Here's an example of the extreme numbers for abundance that are being returned in the posterior draws: N[3,3]=-7.3e+19, N[14,2]= -24922. And several samplers appear to be stuck. Below is the likelihood for counts of abundance, with much of the model being omitted. There is also a survival model and fecundity model that I've omitted here. Why are there negative values for Poisson and binomial?

Thanks in advance for providing very useful software. And apologies if I've goofed on something obvious here, but I've been struggling to get this working for a while now.
Brian

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Slice sampler error with negative values for Poisson and binomial- IPM
parts:
Hi Brian,

My first guess is that there might be an initialization issue.  Are you providing a complete set of inits, including all latent random variables?  Because the issue likely involves the data, constants and inits, we would need a fully reproducible example to examine further.  You can send these off-list if you prefer and we can reply on-list for interested followers.

Here is an example of the kind of problem that could arise.  If the initial values for the various etas and/or omegas (which I can't see defined), happen to make a Poisson parameter or a binomial prob parameter negative, there would be no valid MCMC update.  More subtly, even if one of those parameters is 0, then if the initial value of the declared random variable is non-zero, the model will be initialized with impossible values, giving an initial total log probability of -Inf, making it likely the MCMC will go off the rails.  After building the model, you can inspect it as described in the user manual to see where there may be problematic initial values.  For example,

model$calculate() ## see if the initial log prob of the entire model is -Inf
model$calculate("N[1, 1:10]") ## check log probs of particular part of the model
model$getParam("N[1, 5]", "lambda") ## check what is calculated for this Poisson parameter.
model$eta.BSalpha ## check values in the model

Some other examples of inspecting models can be found in previous nimble-users messages.  

Best,
Perry
